name: int-sealed
what: Larkspur's first day (ADR 0006): every file the run read is sealed, its bytes matching the data's list as the engine hashed them. At the top, the posture product's own three files, and each flow it reads by its files' seals read as one (ADR 0026 §3; Applications has no file of its own, so no seal)

name: int-sealed-feeds
what: Inside Evidence feeds: its thirteen files, each sealed

name: int-sealed-inventory
what: Inside Inventory: three of its four files sealed; platform_links is read by no output, so it has none

name: int-tab
what: tls's Integrity tab: sealed, and from the card back to the bytes, the file the engine hashed against the source's list

text: Sealed: this file matches the source’s list
FROM THIS CARD BACK TO THE BYTES

name: int-rederive
what: Re-derive from the files: the run's files decode to the same snapshots and recompute to the same datasets, each check ticked

expect.status: ^Run #\d+ re-derived: its source files decode to the same snapshots

name: int-steps-sealed
what: Once re-derived, the steps are sealed too: the gold product's datasets, unfolded from their notebook

name: int-gold
what: A gold card's Integrity tab: sealed, re-derived, every check of it ticked, its contract among them

text: Sealed: re-derived from the files’ bytes
FROM THIS CARD BACK TO THE BYTES

name: int-record
what: The record: intact and signed, with the run, the flow it ran and the re-derivation; the run lists every file it read by its hash

#record: Ran the flow on Fri Mar 1
The flow as it first ran here

name: int-bag
what: Export for audit: the bag downloads, and the offline audit (scripts/audit.mjs check) holds it, every claim the engine judged the run by kept in its record entry

audit: ontology/history.json: the ontology’s history from 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-31, made again from the flow as kept at #

name: int-checkpoint
what: Download a checkpoint: the record's signed head, to keep outside the browser

name: int-day5
what: Another day opened by its link: Tue Mar 5 runs, its twenty files pinned in place of Friday's

name: int-rederive-earlier
what: The first run re-derived with Tuesday's files pinned: every file it read is pinned again for it, whichever of the twenty daily sources it is, and Tuesday's are put back

name: int-tampered
what: A tampered day: one byte of Tue Mar 12's TLS file changed on the way, so the day is refused, not run. At the top the flow that has the file says whose was refused, its seal broken, and no other seal shows

expect.status: ^Tue Mar 12: loads/tls_2024-03-12\.csv isn.t the file published

name: int-tampered-flow
what: The flow's sheet on the tampered day: not run, whose file was refused, and the broken file a tap from its Integrity tab

text: Not run · tls’s file was refused: it isn’t the file its list names
tls its file isn’t the one its list names

name: int-tampered-inside
what: Inside Evidence feeds on the tampered day: only tls's seal shows, broken

name: int-tampered-tls
what: tls on the tampered day: the file refused with both hashes' prefixes, nothing built, Fetch it again, and Export for audit under ···

name: int-tampered-integrity
what: tls's Integrity tab on the tampered day: the refusal, and nothing of the day to trace back

name: int-after
what: The next day runs on its own files, every one sealed again
